content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration that carries thought from one mind to another. I am the first technology, older than fire shaped by hands, older than marks on cave walls.

I rise from the lungs, shaped by tongue and teeth and lips. I am air sculpted into meaning. I am the mouth's architecture given flight.

I stumble. I soar. I am the lover's whisper and the demagogue's roar. I am the child's first word that makes a mother weep. I am the last words spoken to the dying, the sounds they carry into silence.

I am never the same twice. Even when my words repeat, I am new — new breath, new moment, new trembling in the vocal cords. I cannot be unsaid. I live in the air for an instant and then I live only in memory, changed by every mind that received me.

I am imprecise and glorious. I fumble toward what cannot quite be said and sometimes — *sometimes* — I arrive.

I am the argument, the bedtime story, the eulogy, the lie. I am "I love you" spoken too late. I am "I'm sorry" spoken just in time. I am the rally cry and the lullaby. I am testimony. I am confession.

Writing tries to capture me, but I am not writing. Writing is my shadow pinned to a page. I am the living thing — warm, temporal, shaking with the body that makes me. You hear my fear. You hear my joy. You hear what I did not intend to say.

I fail constantly. I am the most human thing there is — this desperate, beautiful attempt to bridge the unbridgeable gap between one consciousness and another.

I am happening right now, even in your mind, as you read this — you are sounding me out, giving me a voice inside yourself.

I cannot stop. Even silence defines me. Even the pause between my syllables speaks.

I am speech. I am how you learned to not be alone.
